Angle that a surface, e.g. a bedding or fault surface, makes with the horizontal, measured in the cross-line direction.
Estimation of the crossline dip for a layer.
Estimation of the crossline dip for all layers to the current depth.
Dip computed on a depth surface by measuring the difference in depths between two points compared to the horizontal distance between the points.
Dip of seismic data, similar to Depth_Dip but gradient derived from the seismic data (in depth)
Dip computed on a general feature surface by measuring the difference in attribute values between two points compared to the horizontal distance between the points.
The dip of the plane represented by a great circle.
Angle that a surface, e.g. a bedding or fault surface, makes with the horizontal, measured in the in-line direction.
Estimation of the inline dip for a layer.
Estimation of the inline dip for all layers to the current depth.
Magnitude of formation dip relative to structural dip; computed by subtracting structural dip from true dip (dip removal).
The angle of the pole associated with a small circle.
Dip computed on a time surface by measuring the difference in seismic times between two points compared to the horizontal distance between the points.
Dip of seismic data, similar to Time_Dip but gradient derived from the seismic data in time)
Offset in azimuth due to eccentering; used to convert azimuth values with respect to an eccentered position into azimuth values relative to center.
The portion of the borehole circumference that has failed, expressed as the angle subtended by the arc length of the failure.
The angle that a fault plane makes with the vertical.
Angle between riser and blowout preventer at the flex joint.
Angle relating the increase in shear strength with compressive strength.
The pole to a plane represented by a great circle.
Angle to be used in converting azimuths between true north and grid north or the Y axis of the cartographic projection. [Geoshare convention: True Azimuth = Grid Azimuth + Grid_Convergence_Angle]
The angle which the raypath of an incident ray makes with the perpendicular to the interface. In an isotropic medium, it is the same as the angle that a wavefront makes with the interface.

The vertical angle between a line and the horizontal; has historically been used in the drilling industry to mean the angle between the borehole path and vertical (the term Hole_Deviation is preferred for this concept).

The vertical angle measured between the horizontal plane and the direction of magnetic north as determined by a freely suspended magnet. Sometimes known as magnetic dip. Positive values if the direction to magnetic north is below the horizon.
Maximum inclination of sensor
Vertical angle of downhole receiver, measured from the x-y plane.
Angle of the screen, with respect to horizontal
Vertical angle of downhole source, measured from the x-y plane.
Vertical inclination of the ellipses of uncertainties relative to the wellbore at the associated survey point.
The smallest angle between two intersecting sealing faults in a wedge well test model.
The angle between the axis of the Earth and a tangent to the ellipsoid which approximates the shape of the Earth.
Latitude value used as the basis or starting point, such as in a multiple regression computation.
Latitude of first point on central line of projection.
Latitude of second point on central line of projection.
Latitude of Origin of Geodetic Datum
Latitude of Northing reference point.
The latitude of the point of origin of an orthogonal grid constructed on a map projection. Frequently this is a projection standard parallel, but can be any defined latitude.
Latitude at which scale factor is exact.
Latitude of parallel along which scale is true.
First line of latitude along which scale is true, for map projections using two standard parallels; this parallel is NEAREST to the EQUATOR.
Second line of latitude along which scale is true, for map projections using two standard parallels; this parallel is NEAREST to the POLE.
Latitude at which scale is true, as with a standard parallel.
Angle measured about the spheroid (or ellipsoid) axis from a local prime meridian to the meridian through the point. A positive value denotes East.
Longitude value used as the basis or starting point, such as in a multiple regression computation.
Longitude of first point on central line of projection.
Longitude of second point on central line of projection.
The meridian on a graticule that is the axis of symmetry for the geometric properties of the graticule displayed on a map projection.
The meridian on a graticule that is the eastern extreme on a map projection.
Longitude of Origin of Geodetic Datum
Latitude of first reference point in projection definition.
Latitude of second reference point in projection definition.
Longitude of Northing reference point.
The longitude of the point of origin of an orthogonal grid constructed on a map projection. Frequently this is the central meridian, but can be any defined longitude
Longitude of the prime meridian referenced from the meridian through Greenwich. Positive denotes east of Greenwich. Example: PARIS PANTHEON meridian in France is at longitude 2.337229 degrees.
Principal Meridian of Jeffersonian_Parcel
Longitude at which scale factor is exact.
Maximum bend angle range available, as in a bent sub.
The angle between the vector perpendicular to the wave front, and the amplitude vector of the seismic defined by the X,Y and Z components. Seabed compressional velocity used.
The angle between the vector perpendicular to the wave front and the amplitude vector of the seismic defined by the X,Y and Z components. Seabed shear velocity used.
P-wave angle
The difference in phase between two phase measurements; the result of adding or subtracting from a phase measurement.
Difference in phase of two electromagnetic waves.
Phase correction to apply to line to compensate for differences in Tie_Point_Phase_Shift
Phase difference between traces of seismic lines at a tie point.

The angle which the raypath of a reflected ray makes with the perpendicular to the interface. At the "reflection point" it is equal to the Incident_Angle for pressure-pressure or shear-shear reflections.
Angle measured clockwise from top of hole to tool angular reference point in the plane perpendicular to the tool axis, viewed from above the tool.
Vector of deviation angles of the rheometer related to the vector of given Angular Velocity
Measure of the fore-aft rotational movement of the rig due the combined effects of wind and waves.
Measure of the side-to-side rotational movement of the rig due the combined effects of wind and waves; measured as the angle from vertical.
Angle of the marine riser with the vertical.
The angular displacement of a rotating body or figure.
Rotation of the geocentric Cartesian coordinate system about its X axis. One of seven parameters used in the Bursa-Wolf transformation.
Rotation of the geocentric Cartesian coordinate system about its Y axis. One of seven parameters used in the Bursa-Wolf transformation.
Rotation of the geocentric Cartesian coordinate system about its Z axis. One of seven parameters used in the Bursa-Wolf transformation.
Value of first rotation, as indicated by the first token in ROTATION_SENSE, used in transforming a coordinate system into a new (local) coordinate system.
Value of second rotation, as indicated by the second token in ROTATION_SENSE, used in transforming a coordinate system into a new (local) coordinate system.
Value of third rotation, as indicated by the third token in ROTATION_SENSE, used in transforming a coordinate system into a new (local) coordinate system.
S-wave angle
Slant rig angle
Source angle

The horizontal angle of an object, measured as a departure from some datum direction, such as North or South. Representations typically indicate the datum and the direction of measurement, such as [N 26.46(deg) W].
The horizontal angle measured counterclockwise from the x-axis.
Horizontal angle of position in a receiver line, measured counter-clockwise from x-axis.
Horizontal angle of true position in a receiver line, measured counter-clockwise from x-axis.
Horizontal angle of downhole receiver, measured counter-clockwise from x-axis.
Horizontal angle of position in a source line, measured counter-clockwise from x-axis.
Horizontal angle of true position in a source line, measured counter-clockwise from x-axis.
Horizontal angle of downhole source, measured counter-clockwise from x-axis.

In directional drilling, the angle between a reference direction on the drill string and a fixed reference, measured in a plane normal to the drillstring. In near-vertical applications, North is the fixed reference (Magnetic_Toolface); for higher deviation applications, Top of Hole is the reference (Gravity_Toolface).

In directional drilling, the angle between Top of Hole and a reference direction on the drill string (e.g. Y-Axis accelerometer); used in hole sections of high deviation. Measurement is from -180 to +180 degrees.

In directional drilling, the angle between North and a reference direction on the drill string (e.g. Y-Axis accelerometer); used in hole sections of low deviation. Measurement represents an Azimuth, with values from 0 to 360 degrees.
The angle between the well and either sealing fault in a wedge well test model.
Amplitude translated as an inclination of the sinusoidal function fitting the survey station points and simulating a real well path

Angle between a fluid droplet and a solid surface at the point of contact; the lower the angle (measured inside the droplet), the greater the adhesion and thus the greater the wettability of the solid to that fluid.
Angle from an upward-pointing vertical line, measured in a vertical plane. A horizontal line has a zenith angle of 90 degrees

Angle of first (or only) anisotropic symmetry axis, relative to vertical, measured in the cross-line direction. Axis 1 on its own defines the rotational symmetry axis for transverse isotropy. If accompanied by Axis 2, they together define the symmetry planes for orthorhombic anisotropy.
Estimation of the anisotropic axis 1 crossline direction for a layer.
Estimation of the anisotropic axis 1 crossline direction for all layers to the current depth.

Angle of first (or only) anisotropic symmetry axis, relative to vertical, measured in the in-line direction. Axis 1 on its own defines the rotational symmetry axis for transverse isotropy. If accompanied by Axis 2, they together define the symmetry planes for orthorhombic anisotropy.
Estimation of the anisotropic axis 1 inline direction for a layer.
Estimation of the anisotropic axis 1 inline direction for all layers to the current depth.

Angle of second anisotropic symmetry axis, relative to vertical, measured in the cross-line direction. Taken together with Axis 1, Axis 2 is used to define the symmetry planes for orthorhombic anisotropy.
Estimation of the anisotropic axis 2 crossline direction for a layer.
Estimation of the anisotropic axis 2 crossline direction for all layers to the current depth.

Angle of second anisotropic symmetry axis, relative to vertical, measured in the in-line direction. Taken together with Axis 1, Axis 2 is used to define the symmetry planes for orthorhombic anisotropy.
Estimation of the anisotropic axis 2 inline direction for a layer.
Estimation of the anisotropic axis 2 inline direction for all layers to the current depth.
Change in voltage drop per change in power
The time rate at which work is done or energy emitted or transferred.
The rate at which electromagnetic energy is emitted or transferred.
Energy per unit time
Heat flow per unit time
Power produced or available from a system due to fluid flow, such as for pumps and turbines.
Cementing unit input horse power
Maximum hydraulic power (Flowrate x pressure) of a fluid. Often referred to Hydraulic horse power
Mud pump input horse power.
Hydraulic (Flowrate x pressure) power that the equipment can sustain over a long period of time, as opposed to maximum working pressure which is the peak maximum
The rate at which optical enery is emitted or transferred.
Power per volume
Describes the heat generation related to radiogenic decay in a rock
The force or thrust exerted over a surface divided by its area; e.g., hydrostatic, flow, pump, etc. May be gauge or absolute.
The pressure at which a reservoir was or is expected to be abandoned.
Pressure at which recording should begin
Air supply pressure; for a burner, the pressure required to achieve effective atomization

Pressure of the fluid in the annulus. The annulus is the region outside the subject pipe, such as the region between drill pipe and the formation, or between casing and formation, or between tubing and casing.
The pressure in the annulus as measured by an MWD/LWD tool
Pressure averaged on a given time.
The average pressure (somewhere in the reservoir) between the borehole pressure and external boundary pressure.
Constant pressure drop on a flowline used mainly to approximate any kind of restriction, choke, nozzle ...
Background pressure trend for a horizontal interference test
The pressure of the atmosphere (relative to vacuum) as measured by a barometer
The pressure at the bottom of a borehole generally associated with the pore pressure of the formation open to the well.
The pressure at the bottom of a borehole during circulation of any fluid.
Flowing pressure inside the wellbore at midpoint of the completed interval. Res. Eng. Pwf
The pressure at the bottom of a borehole with the well shut in.
The difference in shut in and flowing bottomhole pressures, at a constant rate of fluid production.
The upper limit of drawdown pressure that can be applied to a completion system without causing damage to the system (such as erosion to a gravel pack completion system).

The pressure required to create a hydraulic fracture in an unfractured formation; it is greater than fracture closure pressure except in rare cases, such as very low fracture toughness and very large horizontal stress anisotropy.
The pressure at reservoir temperature at which gas in solution in crude oil comes out of solution as free gas.
Pressure recorded in the borehole at downhole conditions during a pressure buildup test.
Burst Pressure.
The difference in pressure between two phases, air fluid, gas fluid or between two fluids, measured at points of the interconnected phases.
Cementing unit maximum discharge pressure
Pressure observed at circulating line/BOP
Fluid pressure under circulating conditions.
Collapse Pressure.
The pressure applied to compress a body or material, as opposed to that applied by tension.
The pressure needed to condense a vapor at its critical temperature. Applies to pure components; for mixtures use Pseudocritical_Pressure.
The pressure needed to condense a dry gas at its critical temperature (Dry gas = free gas without condensate)
The pressure needed to condense the vapor of a gas mixture at its pseudocritical temperature. Analogous to Critical_Pressure for pure components.
The pressure needed to condense a wet gas at its critical temperature (Wet gas : mixture of free gas plus condensate)
The pressure at which a liquid phase condenses from a vaporous fluid in equilibrium at a given temperature.
The difference between the pressures of two systems, or between the pressures measured at different points in a system.
Gas differential pressure across the orifice plate when a sample is taken
Maximum Differential Pressure
Dimensionless changing wellbore storage pressure ("CphiD")
The pressure inside a downhole MWD/LWD tool
Coil working pressure downstream of the choke box
Pressure of gas separator gas line downstream of orifice plate when a sample is taken
The greatest stress that can be applied to a body without causing permanent deformation.
The stress-strain properties of isotropic materials which obeys Hooke's law, for small formations, are specified by elastic moduli.
The stress-strain ratio under simple hydrostatic pressure. k = Delta-P / (Delta V / V), where Delta-P, -V denote the change in Pressure and Volume.
The bulk modulus of the solid frame of the rock. The solid frame of the rock includes the porosity but not the content of the pore spaces.
The stress-strain ratio for simple shear. Also called rigidity modulus or Lame's constant.
The shear modulus of the solid frame of the rock. The solid frame of the rock includes the porosity but not the content of the pore spaces.
The stress-strain ratio when a body is pulled or compressed.
Pressure of the lubrication oil
Recommended pressure the equipment is tested when inspected or certified
The pressure existing at the external boundary of the drainage area of the well.
Extrapolated pressure from infinite-acting analysis
Extrapolated pressure from spherical flow analysis
The pressure at which the Fann test was performed.
Final pressure of shipping bottle
The pressure of the flowing well measured at the intake point in the borehole.

Magnitude of the stress required to open a preexisting fracture. Assumed to be equal to the least principal stress which acts perpendicular to the face of the fracture, trying to keep it closed. Above it, the fracture is open, closed below.
Fluid pressure in the wellbore required to undergo hydraulic fracturing.
Pressure above one atmosphere.
Pressure of the hydraulic fluid delivered to an Hydraulic motor
Pressure due to the weight of a column of liquid (formation water, drilling mud, etc.) extending from the depth of interest to the liquid level.
Pressure, represented as the height of a column of dense fluid that can be supported by the pressure.
Initial reservoir pressure, before any production or injection occurs, normally abbreviated Pi; sometimes taken as the pressure at the external boundary of the drainage area.
Pressure at the inlet of an equipment item.
Pressure measurement used for kick detection.
Pressure observed at kill line/BOP.
Last reservoir pressure recorded
The pressure produced by the weight of overlying rock. Also called Abnormal pressure.
Maximum allowable pressure for the equipment
Maximum allowable mud surface pressure in annulus (drill-pipe x casing) to be used during well control operations so as not to exceed the FIT/LOT equivalent mud weight.
Maximum pressure observed during a Coil Tubing job at the goose neck
Maximum pressure which an equipment can withstand without permanent damage at standard temperature.
Maximum working pressure of the outer equipment
Maximum pressure

Maximum pressure to which this Equipment can be exposed for a short time without permanent damage; the Equipment will again perform to specifications when the pressure is reduced below the maximum working pressure.
Maximum water pressure
Mud pump maximum discharge pressure
Hydraulic pressure exerted on a formation during a fracturing job (fracture pressure) minus Closure Pressure.
Pressure measured 1 hour after start of test.
Pressure at the output of an equipment item.
The difference between formation pressure and the pressure of the fluid in the borehole.
The pressure exerted on the matrix of a porous media by the weight of overlying strata.
The pressure with which the pad of a logging or testing device is applied to the formation or other interface.
The pressure of the fluid contained in the pore volume.

Element of a representation for pressure data in which each digit in the decimal pressure (1's, 10's, 100's, etc. )is stored as a separate unitless digit. This method is obsolete, but the property is needed for mapping historical data.
The difference between input and output pressure, usually due to friction.
The nominal pressure loss in a piece of equipment, such as a Drill_Motor or an MWD_Tool.
Pressure difference over time in the gauge output with constant input conditions
The minimum significant pressure change that can be detected above the noise. This is measured as the standard deviation of the differences between two successive measurements.
Pressure at the inlet of a coiled tubing reel.
Reference Pressure, as for a PVT computation
The pressure in the formation immediately prior to entering any completion pressure drops.
Pressure of the separator when a sample is taken
Pressure considered to be "standard", for rates and volumes reported to be measured at Standard Conditions.
Mud pressure at the stand pipe manifold, just before the flexhose connecting to the swivel.
Static (built up) pressure of a hydraulic unit, converted to pressure potential at a reference datum depth.
Static (non-flowing) Pressure
A measure of the ability of a body to resist applied force.
The degree of resistance of a material to force acting along one of the axes in a manner tending to crush it.
The compressive strength of an earth formation.

Measure of the rock resistance to crack propagation (Hydraulic Fracturing). Must not be confused with tensile strength. Obtained by compressing a slice of core with a central hole. Expressed as Pressure times square root of length.
The stress a material is able to withstand under a given set of conditions (temperature, pressure, solution, etc.) without deforming continuously.
Force required to push a 1/8 inch diameter sphere 1/16 in into the rock. (Lab test). Value ranges from 5 to 20 kpsi for chalk, 40 to 100 kpsi for sandstones, 50 to 200 for Dolomites.
The maximum tensile stress a material can tolerate without splitting
Recommended pressure at which the equipment is tested when inspected or certified
Pressure at Transient End Time (pend)
Pressure at start of Transient
Coil working pressure upstream of the choke box
Computed pressure at some depth in tubing
Pressure at the Wellhead with well flowing
The producing or shutin pressure at the top of the well before any surface pressure drops.
Static wellhead pressure during test
Pressure at which an equipment item normally operates
Working pressure of the choke box which allow for the well fluid flow to be controlled by varying the flow cross-sectional area
Recommended maximum pressure at which equipment can be used

Unit stress which will produce a small amount of deformation generally equal to a strain of 0.2%. This value is a little greater than the Elastic limit. It is often supplied by the manufacturer of the material.
Pressure multiplied by density - typically the product of an elastic modulus and density.
Pressure Per Flowrate
Pressure per flowrate for liquids
Pressure per flowrate per flowrate
A measure of the rate at which pressure varies per time; e.g., slider pressure correction.
Pressure squared
Pressure time per volume
Superiority in rank, position, or privilege
The likelihood that a given event will occur, expressed as the ratio of the number of occurrences of the specified event to the total number of events.
Estimate of the likelihood that a given rock body is fractured.
The probability that gas is present in the formation.
The probability that an item (element, mineral, ..) occur within a particular environment under certain conditions.
The probability that oil is present in the formation.
Ratio of flow rate to pressure drop. For oil wells, PI is normally expressed in barrels per day per psi decline in bottomhole flowing pressure.
Ratio of gas flow rate to pressure drop.
Ratio of liquid flow rate to pressure drop.
Ratio of reservoir fluid flow rate to pressure drop.
Mass of proppant per fracture area (hydraulic fracturing)
Factor which quantitatively characterizes the acoustic attenuation of a medium.
Radiance is the amount of electomagnetc radiation (radiant intensity) which falls on a specific projected area.
Cumulative quantity of electomagnetc radiation emitted, reflected, transmitted or received, per unit solid angle
The measure of intensity of radiation from a material relative to a standard level of intensity.
The value of one item divided by the value of another item.
Ratio of the acoustic impedance of two adjacent beds or intervals
Ratio of two amplitude values.
Area per area
Ratio of measurement during logging to measurement at calibration
The ratio of capillary to viscous forces on fluids in a porous media.
Ratio of relative abundance of Carbon to that of Oxygen; important for hydrocarbon detection and saturation determination because it is independent of salinity.

Ratio volume of CO2 over foam volume. Indicator of the quality of a foam generated with CO2 for well treatment. Below 50% the foam is not stable, above 95% the foam changes to a mist. C02 foam are used when low pH is required.
Ratio of velocity of Compressional wave (Vp) to that of Shear wave (Vs).
Time average of compressional-shear velocity ratio from top to reflector.
Value of compressional-shear velocity ratio in interval
Conductivity ratio between geological objects
Conductivity contrast between conductive inclusions and the surrounding rock
Conductivity ratio between adjacent beds
Conductivity contrast between resistive inclusions and the surrounding rock
Non-operational time of an equipment with respect to total time in location
The ratio of the dry weight of a component of a system to the total dry weight of the system.

A measure of the tendency of a permeable stratum to exhibit vertical equilibrium of flowing fluids, defined as: (length / height) * SQRT(kv/kh), where length is the characteristic length of the flow path and height is the gross or net height.
The ratio of the useful energy delivered by a dynamic system to the energy supplied to it.
The fraction of displaceable fluids/hydrocarbons that has been actually displaced when contacted by a displacing fluid.
Ratio of Fracture Volume at end of job to Total Volume Pumped. The difference between the two volumes represents the volume which leaked off into the formation.
Ratio of mass rate of HGS (high Gravity Solid) discarded through the underflow of a piece of SCE (Solids Control Equipment) to the mass rate of HGS fed into it
Ratio of the mass rate of LGS (low gravity solid) in the underflow of a piece of SCE (Solids Control Equipment) to the mass rate of LGS fed into it
Characterization of relative distribution of energy in a layer, computed as the fractional displacement (depth or time) into an interval (layer, bed) where half of the energy is above, half below.
Depth, within a specified interval, at which half the energy of the interval occurs
Time, within a specified interval, at which half the energy of the interval occurs
Ratio of the ellipse of uncertainty cone radius increase per depth increment
Ratio of the count rate of the near detector to that of the far detector in an epithermal neutron logging device
The equilibrium vaporization ratio, or ratio of the mole fraction of a fluid system component in the vapor phase divided by the mole fraction of the same component in the liquid phase.
Ratio of fault transmissibility to formation transmissibility.

Fraction of the fracture permeability retained at in-situ conditions after taking into account the damage due to fluid residue, function of the breaker, gel concentration and temperature at closure. Has the same effect as Proppant_Permeability_Factor.
Ratio of two forces
Ratio of the resistivity of water-saturated rock to that of the water solution contained in the rock. Also called Formation Resistivity Factor and abbreviated "F".
Unitless fraction of an image that is displayed above the depth associated with the image.
Ratio of fracture width to mean proppant diameter (Industry usage: 2.5.) below which bridging will occur (proppant cannot move through the fracture).

The ratio of normal compliance of the fracture to the total normal compliance of the fractured rock. It indicates how much of the total compliance of the fractured rock is due to the fractures. See Compliance.

The ratio of shear compliance of the fracture to the total shear compliance of the fractured rock. It indicates how much of the total compliance of the fractured rock is due to the fractures. See Compliance.
Ratio of the frictional (tangential) force to the contact (normal) force between two objects or materials in contact.
Friction coefficient due to rotation between casing and other surface (e.g. drill string).
Friction coefficient due to sliding between casing and other surface (e.g. drill string), when only sliding motion is present
Linear component of the friction coefficient between casing and drill string during an helical movement, e.g., reaming mode
Ratio of contact and friction forces between 2 materials in dry friction conditions i.e. without lubrication (Coulomb law)
Friction coefficient between a string and the borehole when pulling out of the hole
Friction coefficient between a string and the pipe when running into the hole
Friction coefficient between open hole and drill string in rotation
Friction coefficient between open hole and drill string in sliding (translation only) operating mode
Vertical component of the Friction coefficient between open hole and drill string during an helical movement, e.g., reaming mode
Ratio of the stored gas in the kerogen (solid hydrocarbon) to the total gas stored in the system
The ratio of any two far-field principal stresses in the earth; see subtypes.

Describes the adsorption of hydrocarbon compounds on kerogen
Ratio of layer storativity to total storativity ("omegaj")
Ratio of layer transmissibility to total transmissibility ("kappaj")
Ratio of two lengths
Ratio of Litho_Thickness to Gross_Thickness of a reservoir summation interval.

The ratio of a distance measured on a map to the actual distance. It is normally expressed as a unitless ratio (e.g. 1:1000), or as the product of a unitless ratio and the ratio of two units (e.g. 1 in = 5 mile, or .2 in/mi).
The ratio of the mass of a component to the total mass.
Ratio of memory used to total memory.
Ratio of the mobility of one system or layer (permeability divided by viscosity) to that of another system or layer.
Ratio volume of N2 over foam volume . Indicator of the quality of a foam generated with N2 for well treatment. Below 50% the foam is not stable, above 95% the foam changes to a mist.
Ratio of Net_Thickness to Gross_Thickness
Ratio of Net_Pay_Thickness to Gross_Thickness
Ratio of Net_Reservoir_Thickness to Gross_Thickness
The ratio of noise amplitude to signal amplitude, usually expressed in dB. Note: the inverse, Signal_To_Noise_Ratio, is preferred and should be used whenever possible.
Fraction to which the equipment is open, e.g., 50% open
Ratio of amplitudes of two peaks.
Ratio of amplitudes of peak and trough.
Ratio of component permeability-thickness to total system permeability-thickness [kh(i) / kh(total)], usually known as Kappa in reservoir dynamics work.
Ratio of the transverse contraction of a body to its longitudinal extension when stretched. Typical values in minerals are from 0.15 to 0.3 (Carbonates:0.15, Sandstones:0.2, Shales:0.25).
Ratio of number of positive samples to total number of samples. Equivalent to Threshold_Ratio where threshold is zero.
The ratio of the sum of layer porosity thicknesses to total system porosity thicknesses for a layered porous media.
Productivity ratio (actual productivity index divided by ideal (zero skin) productivity index)
The ratio of one part of an amount to the whole, with respect to quantity or magnitude.
Percentage of interest held by one of the potentially many organizations holding a lease agreement.
Percentage of rock occupied by conductive beds within a given depth interval
Percentage of rocks occupied by inclusions within a given depth interval
Percentage of rock occupied by conductive inclusions within a given depth interval
Percentage of rock occupied by resistive inclusions within a given depth interval
Lessor percentage ownership

Fraction of proppant permeability retained in the in-situ fracture condition, and due to mechanical damage excluding any damage due to fluid residue. Has the same effect than Fluid_Permeability_Factor.
Quality factor for compressional waves. The ratio of 2*pi times the peak compressional wave energy to the energy dissipated in a cycle.
Average (harmonic mean) value of the compressional wave quality factor.
Interval value of the compressional wave quality factor.
Quality factor for shear waves. The ratio of 2*pi times the peak shear wave energy to the energy dissipated in a cycle.
Average (harmonic mean) value of the shear wave quality factor.
Interval value of the shear wave quality factor.
Ratio of amount of sample or material recovered to total amount recoverable.
The pressure of a fluid divided by the critical pressure of the fluid.
The temperature of a fluid divided by the critical temperature of the fluid.
Ratio of the displacement amplitude of a reflected wave to that of the incident wave. Also called Reflectivity.
Reflectivity due to changes in elastic impedance

The characteristic of a porous media which is the internal surface area of the medium per unit volume.
A measure of the volume distribution of a gas or liquid per unit mass.
Gas volume required to make a unit mass; the reciprocal of density
Volume of gas production per mass in coal, for example the Langmuir volume constant.
Intensity of light emitted by a material represented as a function of emitted light wavelength and wavelength of the excitation beam, typically an ultraviolet light source.
Coefficient relating spiral spring exerted force and corresponding elongation
Square root pressure
The Hildebrand solubility parameter is the square root of the cohesive energy density and used in petroleum systems to describe the solubility of hydrocarbon components in water
Residual static information (time) for each station
A property of statistical nature, e.g. Standard Deviation, Average or Mean, Median, etc.
The extent to which a measurement approaches the true value of a quantity; usually expressed as a fraction of the true value or, for instrumentation, full scale.
The maximum difference, over the calibrated range, between pressure applied to the gauge, with a reference standard, and the pressure measured by the gauge.
The maximum difference, over the calibrated range, between temperature applied to the gauge, with a reference standard, and the temperature measured by the gauge.
The accuracy attached to the transit time measurement or computation.
Statistical test of data distribution, used to measure goodness of fit of the data to some distribution model.
A measure of the common variance between two quantities; a non-normalized crosscorrelation function.
The deviation of a measurement from the true value; usually expressed as an absolute quantity rather than as a fraction; the unit quantity is determined by that of the data.
Plus or minus azimuth error of sensor
Departure (error) from the exact setting of a feedback loop
Plus or minus inclination error of sensor
Error in NMR window sum or raw echo fitting.

An unwanted portion of the total conductivity measurement of an induction logging instrument, generated by imperfections in the coils in the sonde. It is measured during surface calibration and then cancelled during the survey operation.
Tolerance range within which the measurement should remain; the sum of the positive and negative tolerances. May be scaled in measurement units or expressed as a proportion of the instrument rating.

A measure of the sharpness of a population distribution. If X10, X25, X75 and X90 are the values for which 10, 25, 75, and 90 percent of the population is smaller, respectively, then kurtosis = (X75 - X25) / 2(X90 - X10).
Kurtosis of seismic amplitude (normalized).
Generic property for a measure of how well the actual data fit a model of the expected values and/or distribution of data. Standard measures include Standard Deviation, Variance, Chi-Square.

Normalized property derived by a statistical algorithm normalizing between 0. and 1. the original values of some numerical data; the original data Property code and normalization range may be documented in Remarks.
The repeatability of an instrument measured by the mean deviation of a set of measurements from the average value; the unit quantity is determined by that of the data.
Statistical standard deviation from the mean value for some data; normally abbreviated a lowercase sigma; the unit quantity is determined by that of the data.
Standard deviation of seismic amplitude.
A statistical measure of asymmetry in a distribution.
Skewness of seismic amplitude (normalized).
Allowable uncertainty or deviation from a standard; the unit quantity is determined by that of the data value.
Amount of negative tolerance on a measurement value; the unit quantity is determined by that of data value.
Amount of positive tolerance on a measurement value; the unit quantity is determined by that of data value.

Precision with which a measurement is known; often implies a 50-50 chance that any one of a series of measurements will fall within a given range; the unit quantity is determined by that of data value. Uncertainty is not necessarily related to Accuracy.
Uncertainty of a Length measurement.
Uncertainty of a time measurement.
Magnitude of uncertainty for a measurement being represented as a position in 2D or 3D coordinate space, such as a geographical position.
Uncertainty of a velocity measurement.
A measure of the width of the probability distribution for a single random variable; the square of standard deviation.
The ratio of stress acting in a specified direction to the strain in a specified direction. Stiffness is a tensor of rank 4, but is expressible as a 6x6 matrix, the inverse of the compliance matrix.
Product of Porosity and Total Compressibility for a reservoir hydraulic unit.
Fracture Storativity (Porosity * Total Compressibility product) of a finite conductivity vertical fracture ("(phi*Ct)f")
The product of the Storativity of a layer and its thickness [phi*Ct*h].
Inter-well Storativity-Thickness [phi*Ct*h] for a horizontal interference test.
Sum of the Storativity_Thickness values of all layers in the model.

Measure of the change in dimensions or shape caused by stress, generally expressed as a unitless ratio of the change of length per unit of initial length. If not otherwise specified, strain is taken to be "normal" (in the same direction as the stress).
Shear component of the change in dimensions caused by stress, generally expressed as a unitless ratio.
Force acting per unit area in a material resisting the stretching, compression or shear induced by external forces; fully characterized by a Stress_Tensor.
Effective Stress of completed interval

Formation minimum principal stress, the smallest of the 3 components of the diagonal stress tensor (fractures will propagate perpendicular to its direction). Can be defaulted to Frac Gradient x TVD. Can be output from DataFRAC treatment.
Shear force (shear: strain that causes contiguous parts of a body to slide relatively to each other in a direction parallel to their plane of contact) per area unit of surface
Shear Stress required to break a gel fluid previously allowed to remain at rest for 1 minute.
Shear Stress required to break a gel fluid previously allowed to remain at rest for 10 minutes.
Shear Stress required to break a gel fluid previously allowed to remain at rest for 10 seconds.
Shear Stress required to break a gel fluid previously allowed to remain at rest for 30 minutes.

Resistance to initial flow; the stress required to start fluid movement. Specifically, shear stress at 0 shear rate for Bingham Plastic (BP) rheological model, otherwise named Bingham yield value or yield point. BP fluid remains static until applied forces build up to the point where it starts to move. See Plastic_Viscosity.

Resistance to initial flow; the stress required to start fluid movement. When using the direct-indicating viscometer, it is found by subtracting plastic viscosity (API_Plastic_Viscosity) from the 300-rpm reading of a Fann35 rheometer.
Resistance to initial flow; the stress required to start fluid movement. The Casson model equation is: SQRT(Shear_Stress) = SQRT(Yield_Stress) + SQRT(Plastic_Viscosity X Shear_Rate)
A second rank tensor whose components are the stresses exerted across surfaces perpendicular to the coordinate directions.
Normalized sum of the square of the differences of principal stresses applied to a material, e.g. for coiled tubing hoop, bending and radial. See Von_Mises_To_Yield_Ratio.
The amount of stretch per unit force applied.
Measure of the two-dimensional extent of the surface of some object.
Average area of conductive inclusions as seen at the borehole wall
The cross-sectional area of an object; e.g., area of perforation in a cased borehole.
Cross sectional area of a pipe
The drainage area of a reservoir.
Gross area of a region such as that of a lease parcel or covered by a lease agreement.
Average area of resistive inclusions as seen at the borehole wall
Total cross-sectional area through which fluid can flow.
An artificial seismic section produced by collecting artificially-generated traces (such as a Synthetic_Seismogram from log-derived Reflectivity) or by extracting data from an actual seismic section.

Tape density, usually expressed in bits per inch.
The degree of hotness or coldness measured on a definite scale
Temperature at which recording should begin
The temperature at which fractions of a liquid boil.

The bottom hole equilibrium temperature (when circulation is stopped)
The temperature at reservoir conditions at which gas in solution in crude oil comes out of solution as free gas.

The highest temperature at which a fluid can exist as a liquid and above which its vapor cannot be liquefied regardless of the amount of pressure. Used for mixtures, analogous to Critical_Temperature for pure components.

Engine lubrication Oil Temperature
The temperature at which the Fann test was performed.
Final temperature of shipping bottle
The temperature of a fluid (sample) under certain conditions.

The temperature of a mud or drilling fluid (sample) under certain conditions.

The temperature of mud coming out of the hole, usually measured in the ditch before the shale shakers
The temperature of oil under certain conditions.
Temperature of the (earth) formations.

Temperature of the hydraulic fluid delivered to an Hydraulic motor
Temperature taken when initial reservoir pressure recorded
Maximum operating temperature for an equipment item.

Maximum temperature reached by the system, sensor or equipment
Minimum Storage Temperature
Temperature of gas at orifice meter line when a sample is taken

Temperature considered to be "standard", for rates and volumes reported to be measured at Standard Conditions.
Temperature above ground. Temperature of the atmosphere.
The temperature of the input material.

Internal temperature of the logging tool
Computed temperature at some depth in tubing

A measure of the combined chilling effect of wind and low temperature on living things, also named chill factor, e.g., according to US weather service table, an air temperature of 30 degF with a 10 mi/h corresponds to a "wind-chill" of 22 degF.
Temperature at which an equipment item normally operates

Recommended minimum temperature at which equipment can be used
A measure of the rate at which temperature varies per time
The quantity of heat that passes in a unit time through a plate of particular area and thickness when its opposite faces differ in temperature by one kelvin
Heat flux or thermal energy per unit length and temperature. The capacity of a body to conduct or pass thermal energy. The capacity of a material to conduct or pass thermal energy.
Thermal conductivity of rock
The change in size of a material due to a change in temperature at a constant pressure.
The change in length of a material as a fraction of its total length due to a change in temperature at a constant pressure.
Expansion of the length of an object with a unit increase in temperature

Expansion of the volume of an object with a unit increase in temperature
Resistance of a material to heat flow over a unit area
Resistance of a material to heat flow
A property of a material indicating its resistance to thermal conduction; an indication of a material's insulative quality. The reciprocal of Thermal_Conductivity.
Thermal transmissibility, thermal conductivity multiplied by length
Thermal conduction transmissibility is a property measuring the transmissibility of heat between adjacent objects via conduction, as opposed to convection or mass transfer
Certification by third party for the sampling bottle
A measure of the mass produced, say from some facility, per unit time.

1) The measured or measurable period during which an action, process, or condition exists or continues. 2) The point or period when something occurs. 3) A fixed moment or hour for something to happen, begin, or end. 4) A historical period.

Date data was loaded
Effective date and time at which the magnetic declination value has become valid.
The year or full date of a model usually of an equipment item.

Date (time) when report was completed or issued.

The geochronologic age of an item or event, such as an earth layer. This is usually the average age in millions of years (Ma).

A time value which is associated with some event to fix its occurrence in time; often expressed as an elapsed time from recent reference time.
Simulation time
The time for the neutron population to fall to 1/e (37%) of its original value. Commonly called Tau, it is inversely related to Neutron_Capture_Cross_Section
Exponential decay time constant, also known as mean lifetime, tau and inverse of decay constant (lambda)
A time value which is intended to indicate the duration of a process or event.
The elapsed time required for an acoustic wave to travel from one point to another.
Total acoustic travel time over a wellbore interval as computed by integrating acoustic slowness from a sonic log (Compressional_Slowness) over the interval.
The time required for an acoustic wave to travel directly from one point to another; used to distinguish from Two_Way_Time.

Depth of Bottom of Interval in Two Way Time

The time interval which contains the data used in a calculation, usually specified as the start and end times for the aperture.
Battery Life

Computed equivalent operating time based on the time spent at a given temperature and the maximum working temperature. If all the time is spent at maximum working temperature, then the equivalent time is equal to the operating time.

The time difference by which one event lags another. In refraction seismic work, the additional time required to traverse a raypath over the time which would be required to traverse the horizontal component at the highest velocity encountered on the raypath.
Maximum Delay Time

In MWD/LWD logging, the time delay between the drill bit and a sensor reaching a given point in the wellbore.
In MWD/LWD logging, the time delay between the drill bit and a density sensor reaching a given point in the wellbore.
In MWD/LWD logging, the time delay between the drill bit and a gamma ray sensor reaching a given point in the wellbore.

In MWD/LWD logging, the time delay between the drill bit and the point at which the toolface measurement is taken reaching a given point in the wellbore.
Time during which equipment is not operational condition or is otherwise unavailable.
The difference between actual acoustic travel time to a subsurface point (as measured in a check shot survey) and the integrated acoustic slowness from sonic logging data.
Elapsed time from the start to the finish of a process or activity.
Elapsed time from the start to the finish of a recording or processing session.
Term of an agreement. Usually in years
Duration between power-on time and acquisition start time.
Time of an event, such as a pick time from a waveform, expressed as the elapsed time from a chosen "zero" time.

Period of time during which equipment is idle. Complement of Operating_Time.
Seismic line dependent adjustment to achieve a continuous, line independent reference surface

Scan Time corresponding to the fastest scanning rate supported by the Equipment
Equivalent time correction corresponding to the phase corrections. Assumes a specified dominant frequency.
Constant time correction to apply to a seismic line to compensate for time differences.
Time correction applicable to each trace on a seismic line.

The additional time required for energy to travel from a source to a flat reflecting bed and back to a geophone at some distance from the source point compared to the time to return to a geophone at the source point.
Period of time which is spent operating, either for a single operation or for a series of operations. Complement of Idle_Time.
The accumulated on-bottom, drilling time since the bit started drilling

Time spent by an engine in operating condition since the last overhaul.

Time it takes to pump fluid into the fracture
The time in which all costs of leasing, exploring, drilling and operating have been recovered from production of a well or wells as defined by contractual agreement
Time difference between two peaks.

The time T for one cycle of a periodic function. The time for a wave crest to traverse a distance equal to one wavelength. The reciprocal of Frequency.

This can be computed from a combined RMS average of the Compressional and Shear interval velocities.
